title: Recorded Simulation of One Step
statement: Let $M$ be a Boolean-input multi-tape machine with state set $Q$, let $T$ be a type of tags, let $upd:T\times\{\text{absent},\text{false},\text{true}\}\to T$, and let $seek$ be a two-tape Boolean machine with states $S$ and designated states $start,finish$. Fix a Boolean input word $x$, a natural-number window radius $s$, a configuration $c$ on $x$, a tag $\tau\in T$, and a record $data$ whose input symbol agrees with the symbol scanned by $c$, whose zero-position flag correctly records whether the input head is at zero, and whose tag is $\tau$. Suppose $c$ lies in the window of radius $s$. Suppose also that a four-tape configuration $d$ records $c$ and $\tau$ on tape $0$ according to the specified record layout, while every other tape is blank. Then there is a time $t\le 40(k+3)(L+1)$, where $k$ is the number of tapes of $M$ and $L$ is the length of the joined record, at which the recording machine reaches the configuration that has verdict state $true$ and whose tape $0$ contains the record of the configuration obtained by applying to $c$ the action prescribed by $M$ from $data$, with its tag updated by $upd$ using that action's output. This run avoids both verdict states before time $t$ and keeps every work-tape head within distance $L+1$ of its initial position through time $t$.
